chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: "Frost on the Moon" feature for Ella, Jordan and Linton
summary: They created a vocal trio feature for the Apollo and discussed how each singer's feature was planned.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And we had Ella. Now we had picked -- it was a song that we liked very well. And we decided to let the three of them do it. Do a duet on it. They could use it on the stage, they could use it on one nighters, and things like that, in the show.

"Frost On The Moon." This is one of the things that we featured in the Apollo Theater. Louie Jordon, Ella, and Charlie Linton.
And he sang some pretty ballads. He didn't do too much singing. He probably sang maybe every other set.
Sometimes he would sing two numbers on a set, or something like that, when it was his time to do one up, you know.
He was a very good singer. Nice looking fella. Looked like an Indian. And he could sing good.
And when Louie Jordon come in, we decided to do Frost On The Moon like a trio thing.
I think Van Alexander wrote that. Yeah, I think he wrote that, because it was a pop thing. I liked it and I (inaudible) trio.

See, all these things were discussed before we even told anybody what they were going to do. All these things were discussed with myself, Chick and maybe Sampson -- whoever -- (inaudible) the other arrangers around. We discussed these things,
